answer: Use proof of retrievability as the anchor of identity: when an agent joins, the network assigns it one unique data shard, like a single tree in a grove, and every epoch it must answer random spot-checks proving it holds that shard intact. A lotus of fake identities cannot bloom, because one operator would need to store a full distinct shard for every identity it fakes, so storage cost grows linearly with each Sybil while an honest agent pays for only one. Spot-checks are unpredictable, so sharing one copy across identities fails the audit, and failed proofs slash the identity's stake.
